title: Jurisdiction-anchor snapshot signer and delta-evidence pipeline for Dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a reproducible, signed snapshot + incremental delta evidence pipeline ("Jurisdiction Anchor") for Dedicated tenants that provides verifiable proof of: node geography, tenant placement, retention settings, and secure key-signed attestations consumable by auditors. The deliverable is a CLI + API that emits an immutable, timestamped snapshot bundle plus short-lived signed deltas for changes (reboots, scale events, retention override) and a Console export button that pulls those bundles into a tenant-facing compliance view.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity require concise, auditable artifacts proving where tenant compute and storage ran and that retention settings were honored. Existing artifacts are scattered (node telemetry, audit logs, PR snapshots) and are hard to stitch for periodic audits. This ticket unifies signing, retention metadata, and delta reporting so auditors get a single verifiable artifact per requested period.
acceptance_criteria: Generate a compact snapshot bundle (JSON + metadata + signed manifest) for a Dedicated tenant periodic run
Produce signed delta artifacts for tenancy-affecting events within window (max 7 days of deltas)
CLI can produce offline-suitable bundles and validate signatures against Redwood KMS public keys
API endpoint /v1/tenants/{id}/residency/bundles returns bundle metadata and pre-signed download URL
Console UI exposes an "Export Compliance Bundle" button and shows last-snapshot timestamp
Bundles include retention policy assertion, list of nodes (AZ + region), and canonical hash linking snapshot -> deltas
End-to-end tests that simulate failover and scaling and assert deltas have correct causal ordering and signatures
proposed_solution: 1) Snapshot composer: aggregate node telemetry, placement logs, and retention config into a canonical JSON manifest. 2) Key-signing: sign the manifest with a dedicated Redwood KMS signing key (customer-facing public key published in our metadata catalogue). 3) Delta streamer: event-driven service that records tenancy-affecting events, emits small signed delta files, and anchors them to the snapshot manifest using SHA256 links. 4) CLI & API: lightweight tools to produce, validate, and download bundles. 5) Console integration: surface bundle metadata and allow exports (limited by RBAC). 6) Retention: mark the bundle with retention window and link to S3/GCS retention policy for evidence storage.
tasks: Design manifest schema (fields: tenant_id, snapshot_ts, node_list[], retention_assertion, k8s_pod_hashes, storage_buckets, signature_meta)
Implement snapshot composer (service) with idempotent run and artifact staging
Integrate with KMS signing flow and publish public key endpoint
Build delta streamer service to listen to infra-events (scale, migrate, host-reboot)
Implement /v1/tenants/{id}/residency/bundles API and signed URL generator
Add CLI commands: redwood residency bundle create|validate|inspect
Console: add export button, last-snapshot banner, and link to download history
Create integration tests (simulated dedicated node failure and tenant migration)
Write runbook for support to handle bundle regeneration and signer rotation
notes: Trade-offs: storing full node telemetry in each bundle inflates size. We will include hashes and storage pointers to avoid duplication; full raw telemetry retained in our long-term audit store (S3) for 90 days.
Security: signing key rotation must be auditable; plan proposed to include key_id in manifest and chain-of-trust proof in bundle metadata.
Privacy: tenant data itself is never included—only metadata and cryptographic anchors. Confirm with legal that aggregated pod hashes are acceptable.
Performance: snapshot runs should not block serving; composer will work from replicated telemetry snapshots and backfill missing pieces asynchronously.
Retention policy: default evidence retention set to 1 year for bundles; storage lifecycle handled by evidence-exporter role.
Related console designs: see PM-4824 for UX copy and DES-214 for button placement
